Salman Khan & others, Case No.- 2773/2023, arising out of Case Crime No. 589/2021, Under Sections 498A/323/504/506 I.P.C., Police Station- Thakurganj, District - Lucknow and the charge sheet dated 01-11-2022 pending before Learned A.C.J.M C.B.I. (A.P.) Lucknow, in pursuance therefore, in the interest of justice."

entities.text: State.......v/s.... Salman Khan & others, Case No.- 2773/2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. In this case, the petitioners have initially filed Petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. bearing Application U/S 482 No.3520 of 2023 wherein this Court vide order dated 12.4.2023 directed the parties to appear before the trial court concerned and the trial court was directed to verify the contents and parties of the compromise deed.

4. In compliance of the aforesaid order, compromise deed was filed before the learned Court below i.e. Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, C.B.I. (A.P.), Lucknow, who vide order/ report dated 13.07.2023 has verified the contents and parties of the compromise deed and submitted report to the extent that the parties and contents of the compromise deed are genuine and they have entered into the compromise by free-will.

entities.text: Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, C.B.I. (A.P.),
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 has submitted that the parties in dispute are not interested to pursue the criminal case.

6. The Apex Court in re: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala, reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343, has observed that even if the offence(s) in question is / are not compoundable within the scope of Section 320 Cr.P.C. even then considering the facts and circumstances of the case in question the Constitutional Court may allow the parties to compound such offence(s) on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

entities.text: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala, reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

7. Not only the above, considering the facts and circumstances of the issue in question and other dictums of the Apex Court in re: B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; 2003 (4)
SCC 675, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303; State of Rajasthan vs. Shambhu Kewat,
(2014) 4 SCC 149; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Deepak (2014) 10 SCC 285; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Manish (2015) 8 SCC 307; J.Ramesh Kamath vs. Mohana Kurup (2016) 12 SCC 179; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Rajveer Singh (2016) 12 SCC 471 and Parbatbhai Ahir vs. State of Gujarat (2017) 9 SCC 641, the entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case are hereby quashed on the basis of compromise.
